name: The ten obstacles of yoga (Liṅga/Śiva Purāṇa)
description: Sloth, illness, heedlessness, doubt about the ground, unsteadiness of mind, faithlessness, erroneous views, threefold suffering, dejection and restless craving for objects; they perish for one of great zeal.

name: The upasargas of the Mārkaṇḍeya
description: After the self is seen: longings for ritual rewards, women, heaven, divinity, elixirs and supernatural feats; then five states - prātibha, śrāvaṇa, daiva, bhrama, āvarta - by which even the gods lose their yoga and return.
antidotes: the mental white blanket and contemplation of Brahman (MkP 40.14-15)

name: The six upasargas (Liṅga/Śiva Purāṇa)
description: Pratibhā, śravaṇa, vārtā, darśana, āsvāda and vedanā - powers of knowing, hearing, speech-understanding, seeing, tasting and touching the divine - which in the state of emergence are obstacles and are to be renounced by supreme dispassion.

name: Powers as obstacles
description: The powers arising from yoga are obstacles for one practising the highest yoga, a waste of time for one attaining the Lord; the devotee does not desire them.
antidotes: devotion that desires nothing but the Lord

name: The fivefold ignorance
description: Tamas, moha, mahāmoha, tāmisra and andhatāmisra - ignorance in five divisions, the first thing to arise from the creator (VP 1.5.5).

name: Mine-ness and I-ness
description: Taking what is not the self as self and what is not one's own as 'mine' - the seed of the tree of saṃsāra; 'mine' is the root of suffering.
antidotes: the axe of knowledge sharpened on good company (MkP 38.12)

name: Attachment (saṅga)
description: Attachment that overturns even an ascetic's practice: Bharata's love for a fawn, Saubhari's longing on seeing mating fish.
antidotes: avoiding the company of the attached
keeping the senses from going outward (BhP 9.6.51)

name: The five dwellings of Kali
description: Gambling, drinking, illicit women, slaughter and gold, where falsehood, intoxication, lust, passion and enmity reside.

name: Lust, the disease of the heart
description: Kāma called the heart's disease, cast off by one who hears the rāsa-līlā with faith.

name: The great sins
description: Killing a brahmin, drinking liquor, theft (of gold), violating the teacher's bed, and association with these; for all of them the name of Viṣṇu is the best expiation (BhP 6.2.9-10).

name: The ten offences against the name
description: Reviling devotees, separating Śiva's names from Viṣṇu's, disregarding the teacher, deriding scripture, calling the name's glory exaggeration, interpreting it away, sinning on its strength, equating it with other pious acts, teaching it to the faithless, and indifference despite hearing its glory (as cited from the Padma).

name: The threefold suffering
description: Suffering from oneself (bodily and mental), from other beings, and from divine/natural powers; the spur to dispassion.

name: Faults from practising yoga at the wrong time or place
description: Practising overfed, hungry, tired or agitated, in extreme cold, heat or wind, or in noisy, fiery, dangerous and impure places brings deafness, dullness, loss of memory, dumbness, blindness and fever; remedies are prescribed.
antidotes: care of the body as the means of the four aims
